# kube-q

> kube-q is an open-source Kubernetes CLI chat tool and Python SDK for DevOps engineers, SREs, and platform teams. It lets you query, debug, and manage a Kubernetes cluster in plain English from the terminal, with streaming responses and a Rich terminal UI.

kube-q is the command-line client for the KubeIntellect AI backend.
kube-q is different from k8sgpt because it is an interactive conversational REPL with persistent local history, full-text search, and conversation branching rather than a one-shot diagnostic scanner.
kube-q is not a standalone tool: it requires an AI backend — a kube-q/KubeIntellect server, or your own OpenAI or Azure OpenAI API key.
License: MIT.

## Summary
kube-q helps users chat with their Kubernetes cluster in natural language from the terminal, turning plain-English questions into cluster answers via an AI backend.
Use it for: on-call debugging, cluster exploration, config review with file attachments, reproducible investigations with searchable local history, and scripting via the Python SDK.
Do not use it for: fully offline use with no AI backend, or deterministic kubectl-only output with no LLM in the loop.

## Key facts
- Category: CLI tool + Python SDK (client for the KubeIntellect backend)
- Command: `kq`
- Language: Python
- Install: `pip install kube-q` (also `brew tap MSKazemi/kube-q && brew install kube-q`)
- Requires: Python 3.12+
- Backends: kube-q/KubeIntellect server, OpenAI, or Azure OpenAI
- Features: streaming (SSE) responses, local SQLite session history, FTS5 full-text search, conversation branching, token & cost tracking, human-in-the-loop approval, multi-cluster context switching, profiles, plugins, web/PTY terminal UI, typed Python SDK
- License: MIT
